hero.title: Order Ranking
hero.description: Order Ranking is a high-yielding scoring topic in the General Aptitude and Reasoning section of the Allahabad High Court RO/ARO and UPPSC examinations. It evaluates a candidate's ability to deduce positions, ranks, heights, weights, and sequences of individuals or objects based on given comparative data and conditional statements.

items.title: Total Count Memory Rule
items.decryption: L + R - 1: Always remember to subtract 1 to avoid double counting the target person.

items.title: Inequality Chain Rule
items.decryption: CCC: Connect common variables first, then compare extremities to establish absolute order.

items.question: In a row of 40 students, Rohan is 15th from the left. What is his rank from the right end?
If Aman is 10th from the top and Priya is 21st from the bottom in a class, and there are 5 students between them, what is the maximum total strength?
items.answer: Maximum Total = Top Rank + Bottom Rank + Persons Between = 10 + 21 + 5 = 36.

items.question: Why do we subtract 1 when calculating total persons from a single person's left and right ranks?
items.answer: Because the individual is counted twice—once when counting from the left and once from the right.

items.question: What condition indicates an overlapping row in ranking problems?
items.answer: When the sum of ranks of two individuals from opposite ends is greater than the total number of persons.

traps.title: Common Exam Traps to Avoid
items: Double Counting Trap: Failing to subtract 1 when calculating total strength from a single person's coordinates, leading to an inflated answer by exactly 1.
Ignoring Overlap Conditions: Applying standard non-overlapping formulas when the sum of ranks exceeds total strength, resulting in negative or impossible intermediate values.
Directional Reversal Confusion: Confusing 'from the left' with 'from the right' or mixing up ground-floor numbering with top-down building sequences.

deepDive.title: Order Ranking Core Study Notes
deepDive.description: Order Ranking is a high-yielding scoring topic in the General Aptitude and Reasoning section of the Allahabad High Court RO/ARO and UPPSC examinations. It evaluates a candidate's ability to deduce positions, ranks, heights, weights, and sequences of individuals or objects based on given comparative data and conditional statements.

sections.title: Fundamental Formulas and Linear Ranking
sections.content:
Mastering single-row and multi-row positional counting is essential for solving basic to intermediate ranking problems efficiently.

  • Total Persons in a Row: When a person's rank from the left (L) and right (R) is given, Total = (L + R) - 1, because the person is counted twice.
  • Finding Rank from Opposite End: Right Rank = (Total - Left Rank) + 1. Conversely, Left Rank = (Total - Right Rank) + 1.
  • Persons Between Two Individuals (Non-Overlapping): If sum of ranks from both ends is less than total persons, Persons Between = Total - (Sum of two given ranks).
  • Maximum Persons in a Row: Maximum capacity occurs when there is no overlapping between the given positions: Max = Rank1 + Rank2 + Persons between them.

sections.title: Interchanging Positions Concept
sections.content:
Advanced questions frequently feature two individuals swapping their positions and resulting in new calculated ranks.

  • Swap Mechanics: When Person A and Person B interchange positions, A takes B's former position while maintaining relative structural order.
  • Finding Total Strength via Swap: Total = (Person A's new position from one end) + (Person B's old position from the other end) - 1.
  • Calculating Shift Difference: The change in numerical rank for one person after interchange equals the change for the other person.
  • No Overlap Check: Always verify that the sum of new and old positions does not violate basic ordinal sequence logic before finalizing answers.

sections.title: Comparison Based Ranking (Height, Weight, Age)
sections.content:
Inequality-based ranking problems require systematic symbol translation using greater than (>) and lesser than (<) operators.

  • Inequality Symbol Convention: Use standard directional inequalities: A > B means A is heavier, taller, or older than B.
  • Combining Statements: Link common entities across statements (e.g., if A > B and B > C, combine as A > B > C) to form a unified chain.
  • Extremities Identification: Quickly identify absolute tallest/heaviest (never appearing on the smaller side) and shortest/lightest.
  • Handling Conditional Constraints: Pay close attention to restrictive modifiers like 'only', 'at least', 'not more than', and 'second from the top'.

sections.title: Advanced Puzzles & Matrix Ranking
sections.content:
High-level RO/ARO exams incorporate multi-parameter matrices linking ranks with grades, professions, or scores.

  • Matrix Grid Formation: Construct a tabular grid assigning rows to individuals and columns to attributes like rank, score, and department.
  • Elimination Technique: Cross out impossible combinations systematically using negative clues (e.g., 'A does not secure 1st rank').
  • Floor & Building Ranking: Note whether numbering starts from ground floor (1st) upwards or top floor downwards to avoid directional errors.
  • Time Management Strategy: Skip convoluted multi-statement ranking puzzles in the first pass and revisit them during the review phase.
